candidate_atomics.name: centralize-provider-client-configuration
candidate_atomics.title: Configure the provider client at application startup
candidate_atomics.description: Expose the provider's optional connection and routing settings at the application boundary and apply only supplied values to the shared client before downstream components are created.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a compatible provider endpoint to receive its required client configuration without embedding that configuration in the domain component constructor.
semantic_action.module_role: application composition and provider-client configuration boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The application accepts only key and base settings, while the domain component constructor owns provider-module initialization and forces a default base value.
semantic_action.post_state: The application boundary accepts the supported optional provider settings and initializes the shared provider client before constructing downstream components; omitted optional settings are not overwritten.
semantic_action.validation: Parse representative provider arguments or configuration fields and verify the corresponding provider-client attributes are set before domain-component construction, while omitted values remain untouched.

candidate_atomics.name: decouple-domain-construction-from-provider-credentials
candidate_atomics.title: Remove provider credentials from domain-component construction
candidate_atomics.description: Make domain-component creation independent of provider initialization after configuration ownership moves to the application boundary, then reconcile all direct construction call sites.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent provider-specific credentials and endpoint defaults from leaking into the constructor contract of the component that manages editing behavior.
semantic_action.pre_state: Every direct component construction requires an API key and optionally a base URL, and construction mutates the global provider client.
semantic_action.post_state: The component constructor requires only its domain inputs and no longer mutates provider configuration; direct call sites conform to that contract.
semantic_action.validation: Instantiate the component through the updated production and test call sites without provider credential arguments and run the existing constructor-dependent regression tests.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-provider-routing-at-request-dispatch
candidate_atomics.title: Forward provider-specific routing fields at request dispatch
candidate_atomics.description: Translate configured routing identifiers into the keyword arguments expected by the provider's request method, without adding absent optional fields.

semantic_action.intent: Route chat requests through providers that require a deployment identifier or engine argument while preserving ordinary requests when those settings are absent.
semantic_action.pre_state: Request dispatch sends the common chat-completion fields but cannot express provider-specific deployment or engine routing.
semantic_action.post_state: Each request includes deployment_id and/or engine exactly when the corresponding configured client attributes exist, and otherwise retains the common request shape.
semantic_action.validation: Mock the provider request method and assert configured routing attributes appear under the provider's expected request keys, with separate assertions that absent attributes produce no extra keys.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-compatible-provider-configuration-and-routing
candidate_workflows.title: Adapt a compatible provider across configuration, construction, and request boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for adding provider-specific client settings and request-routing fields while keeping domain construction independent of credentials and preserving the default request path.

workflow_graph.goal: Accept the compatible provider's required settings at the application boundary and translate them into the client and request interfaces needed to dispatch a chat completion successfully.
when_to_use: A provider uses an otherwise compatible client library but requires additional endpoint metadata or routing identifiers.
Provider configuration is currently split into or coupled with a domain-component constructor.
The provider request method accepts routing fields that are not represented in the application's common request construction.
anti_goals: Do not redesign model prompting, edit formats, retry policy, or response processing.
Do not force provider-specific optional values into requests when the user did not configure them.
Do not retain credentials in unrelated domain constructor signatures merely to initialize a shared provider client.
Do not claim end-to-end provider connectivity without a request-level or integration oracle.
not_applicable_when: The provider is not compatible with the existing client and request/response protocol.
The required adaptation changes authentication or transport semantics beyond client attributes and request keyword mapping.
Provider configuration is intentionally isolated per component or per request and cannot safely use the shared client state evidenced here.
inputs: provider request method's expected routing argument names
workflow_graph.entry_state: The application can configure a key and base endpoint, but additional provider settings cannot flow through the interface; provider initialization is coupled to domain construction; and request dispatch omits provider-specific routing fields.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Supplied provider settings are applied before domain construction, the domain constructor is provider-independent, and request dispatch conditionally carries the provider's expected routing identifiers without changing the ordinary request path.

steps.condition: The compatible provider exposes additional client-level configuration values.
steps.validation: Verify each supplied interface value maps to the correct client attribute before component creation and that omitted optional values are not assigned.

steps.condition: Provider initialization previously occurred inside the domain-component factory or constructor.
steps.validation: Verify production and direct test call sites construct the component without credential or endpoint arguments and retain existing behavior.

steps.condition: The provider requires deployment or engine routing fields on each request.
steps.validation: Capture the provider request call and verify configured routing fields are translated to deployment_id and engine, while absent fields remain absent.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: confirm the supported interface fields map to provider-client attributes and the domain constructor no longer owns provider initialization.
Constructor regression check: run existing domain, command, and editing tests through the simplified construction contract.
Request-unit check: mock the provider request method and assert routing-key presence and absence for configured and unconfigured cases.
Configuration-path check: exercise command-line and configuration-file inputs to confirm equivalent normalized client state.
Integration check: issue a minimal request against a configured compatible provider endpoint and confirm successful routing.
stop_conditions: Stop if the provider client does not support the proposed client attributes or request arguments.
Stop if configuration ownership cannot be moved without introducing conflicting shared-client state.
Stop if existing direct construction call sites cannot be reconciled to the provider-independent contract.
Defer completion if no oracle can verify the emitted request arguments or a real compatible-provider request.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned change contains no direct automated assertion for client-attribute assignment or deployment_id/engine forwarding.
The changed regression tests could not be executed in the supplied environment because pytest is not installed.
Successful live connectivity to the documented compatible provider is not established by the checkout or evidence bundle.
The shared mutable provider-module state may affect multiple component instances; the pinned change does not test isolation or reset behavior.

unresolved_questions: Did pull request 88 pass its historical CI suite? The supplied GitHub bundle omits status checks, and the local environment cannot run pytest.

Does the target client version accept both deployment_id and engine simultaneously, or are they alternative routing modes? The implementation forwards both when both attributes exist, but no test or discussion resolves the intended precedence.

Are environment-variable forms for the newly added options expected to be part of the supported contract through configargparse's automatic prefix behavior? The implementation makes that plausible, but the pinned change does not document or test those names.

title: Restore resumed sessions through the canonical persisted provider route
before: At parent commit 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the Desktop/TUI resume reader independently extracted only top-level provider, base_url, and api_mode values from model_config, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not inspect model_config.gateway_runtime, even though the messaging gateway persisted the most recently executed route there on each turn. Consequently, after a session changed providers, Desktop resume could combine the stored model with a stale first-call billing provider or stale top-level endpoint and wire settings.
after: At commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, Desktop/TUI resume delegates persisted-route selection to the same SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime reader used by CLI resume. That reader prioritizes a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime route, otherwise retains top-level provider/base_url/api_mode data and fills only a missing provider from a routable billing_provider. Existing downstream endpoint-safety, provider-healing, reasoning, and service-tier handling remains in the Desktop resume path.
diff: The change removes the duplicate route-selection logic and local bare-billing-provider import from tui_gateway/server.py, calls SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row), and converts its provider/base_url/api_mode result into resume overrides. It adjusts the canonical reader so billing_provider supplements, rather than loses to, partial top-level route metadata. Two regression tests establish that nested gateway_runtime wins over both a stale first-call billing_provider and stale top-level route keys, while existing tests cover nested/top-level precedence, invalid metadata, bare billing buckets, and routable billing-provider fallback.

title: Adapt replayed reasoning messages to a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint
before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, provider selection had no endpoint-specific adapter for api.fireworks.ai. Requests therefore used the default OpenAI-compatible provider, which, for model names containing qwen3, copied each non-empty assistant reasoning_content value into an additional reasoning field. The pipeline sent that provider-built request outbound, so a multi-turn continuation replaying a thinking response carried both fields to an endpoint that rejects messages[N].reasoning with HTTP 400.
after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, exact api.fireworks.ai hosts and their subdomains select a dedicated provider. It first retains the default request construction, then creates an outbound message array that removes reasoning only from assistant messages where reasoning is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content. It preserves reasoning_content, distinct caller-supplied reasoning values, source history, and the existing default behavior for other endpoints.
diff: The change adds and exports an endpoint-specific provider, inserts hostname-based selection before the default-provider fallback, and overrides outbound request construction to undo only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror. It also adds focused routing and transformation tests plus an HTTP integration test that exercises two-turn history conversion through the real generator/provider path against a strict local endpoint.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a resolves issue #11657 through PR #11701 and identifies the failure as an HTTP 400 caused by a mirrored reasoning field on replayed Qwen3 thinking turns.

In the parent state, DefaultOpenAICompatibleProvider.buildRequest detects qwen3 in the request model and maps assistant messages through mirrorReasoningContentToReasoning, which copies a non-empty reasoning_content value into reasoning when reasoning is not already a string.
ContentGenerationPipeline delegates the converted request to this.config.provider.buildRequest before the request proceeds through later wire-shape processing.

The dedicated provider calls the default provider first and then maps the resulting messages through unmirrorReasoningField, placing compatibility adaptation at the outbound provider boundary.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent strict endpoints from rejecting replayed structured messages while retaining the information they accept and preserving caller-authored values.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt_shared_request_shape_for_strict_endpoint
candidate_workflows.title: Adapt a shared request shape for a stricter compatible endpoint
candidate_workflows.description: Route only the affected endpoint to a narrow outbound adapter, then remove the provably derived incompatible field while preserving shared behavior and caller data.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow multi-turn replay through a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint without sending a shared-layer compatibility field that the endpoint rejects.
when_to_use: A nominally compatible endpoint rejects a field synthesized by shared request construction rather than supplied independently by the caller.
The failure occurs after prior structured assistant output is replayed, including continuations following thinking or tool-use turns.
The endpoint can be identified from configuration using a canonical hostname boundary.
anti_goals: Do not remove the accepted source field needed to replay prior reasoning.
Do not disable or change shared mirroring behavior for endpoints that accept or require it.
Do not infer endpoint identity from a hosted model-family name.
Do not mutate persisted or caller-owned conversation history.
Do not discard a distinct explicit field merely because it has the same semantic category as the rejected derived field.
not_applicable_when: The endpoint itself requires the derived field or rejects the source field instead.
The rejected value cannot be distinguished from a caller-authored value using an evidence-backed invariant.
Provider identity cannot be established safely from available configuration.
The failure is unrelated to outbound request shape or multi-turn replay.
inputs: Canonical hostname contract for the affected endpoint
Endpoint rejection payload or equivalent reproduced failure
Representative multi-turn history containing the structured assistant field
workflow_graph.entry_state: A shared provider emits both a source field and its synthesized mirror during replay, and requests to one strict endpoint fail before continuation completes.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Only requests routed to the affected endpoint omit the exact synthesized field at the outbound boundary; accepted fields and explicit distinct values survive, other endpoints retain prior behavior, and multi-turn continuation succeeds.

steps.condition: The selected endpoint rejects the derived field and the shared transformation makes the derived copy recognizable by exact equality with its source.

title: Safely adapt SDK endpoint options to the selected provider interface
before: At parent c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40, the content-generator configuration could carry an explicit baseUrl, and client creation forwarded that value directly to GoogleGenAI. It did not read the provider-specific GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL environment variables, did not validate custom endpoint URLs, and passed config.vertexai through unchanged, leaving it undefined when the authentication type identified a provider but credential inference had not populated the flag.
after: At cb289e0724b46ce867b6d3fe4bd0ac6ed890dc45, GoogleGenAI client creation first prefers an explicit baseUrl, otherwise selects the environment endpoint associated with the authentication type, validates any selected custom endpoint as a URL and requires HTTPS except for localhost loopback hosts, forwards the accepted endpoint through httpOptions.baseUrl, and derives the SDK vertexai mode from the Vertex authentication type when the explicit flag is absent. Tests cover both provider branches, explicit-over-environment precedence, provider selection without inferred credentials, localhost HTTP, malformed URLs, and insecure remote HTTP.
diff: The implementation added a custom-endpoint validator and provider-aware endpoint resolution inside the GoogleGenAI construction branch. It replaced direct config.baseUrl forwarding with explicit-first, authentication-directed resolution from two environment variables; rejected malformed or insecure remote endpoints; and changed the SDK mode argument from config.vertexai to config.vertexai ?? (authType is the Vertex branch). The test suite added seven focused cases and updated existing SDK-constructor expectations to require a concrete false mode for the non-Vertex branch. Documentation added the two environment contracts and their transport restrictions.

title: Prefer endpoint-specific credentials across OpenRouter resolution paths
before: At parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, both the CLI's eager initialization path and the shared OpenRouter runtime resolver selected an explicit key first, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY. When both environment variables existed, an OpenRouter request could therefore receive the OpenAI credential and fail authentication.
after: At merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a, both resolution paths select an explicit key first, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then OPENAI_API_KEY. The shared resolver retains OPENAI_API_KEY as a compatibility fallback when the endpoint-specific key is absent, and regression tests encode both the preferred-key and fallback branches.
diff: The implementation swaps two environment-variable lookups in cli.py and hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py without changing explicit-key precedence or base-URL resolution. tests/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py adds two tests: one proving OPENROUTER_API_KEY wins when both variables are set and one proving OPENAI_API_KEY remains the fallback when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent. Overall first-parent diff: 3 files changed, 34 insertions, 2 deletions.

episode.title: Prefer endpoint-specific credentials across OpenRouter resolution paths
episode.before: At parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, both the CLI's eager initialization path and the shared OpenRouter runtime resolver selected an explicit key first, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY. When both environment variables existed, an OpenRouter request could therefore receive the OpenAI credential and fail authentication.
episode.after: At merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a, both resolution paths select an explicit key first, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then OPENAI_API_KEY. The shared resolver retains OPENAI_API_KEY as a compatibility fallback when the endpoint-specific key is absent, and regression tests encode both the preferred-key and fallback branches.
episode.diff: The implementation swaps two environment-variable lookups in cli.py and hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py without changing explicit-key precedence or base-URL resolution. tests/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py adds two tests: one proving OPENROUTER_API_KEY wins when both variables are set and one proving OPENAI_API_KEY remains the fallback when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent. Overall first-parent diff: 3 files changed, 34 insertions, 2 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: Merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a has first parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, merges PR #295, and states that it fixes issue #289 by resolving OPENROUTER_API_KEY before OPENAI_API_KEY in all code paths.

The implementation-side parent commit explains the failure: when both variables were set, the wrong key was sent to OpenRouter, causing authentication failures; it identifies cli.py and runtime_provider.py as the corrected paths.
Before the change, the CLI constructor initialized its API key as explicit api_key, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

title: Allow keyless cloud authentication without changing the configured principal
before: At parent c2d63fbe582a3d37051816dea4775687a4ab9896, both the CLI authentication preflight and core model validation rejected the selected cloud-hosted auth mode whenever no API key resolved. Supplying a placeholder key was unsafe because the SDK interpreted any key as an alternate express authentication mode. Client construction also depended on an environment-variable side effect to select the cloud endpoint, so startup paths that skipped that side effect could target the wrong endpoint.
after: At fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430, a nonblank project configuration permits the keyless default-credential path only when the selected provider entry does not declare its own key variable. Missing-credential messages describe the keyless alternative only where applicable, while status preflight reports the unverified default-credential state as unknown rather than claiming a token exists.
diff: The change adds a shared, whitespace-aware project predicate; makes CLI and core credential gates accept eligible project-only configurations; preserves declared key-variable authority; explicitly selects cloud SDK mode from the auth type; keeps absent keys undefined; adds conditional default-credential guidance to errors; and represents keyless preflight status as indeterminate. Tests cover eligible and excluded configurations, missing project behavior, whitespace, strict validation, endpoint-mode construction, key absence, and preflight status.

commit.subject: fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials (#9017)
commit.body_excerpt:
* fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials

Vertex AI auth required an API key, so an ADC or service account setup
could not start. Supplying a placeholder to satisfy the check made it
worse: an explicitly passed key switches the Google SDK to Vertex
Express mode, which clears the project and location and rejects the
request with "API keys are not supported by this API".

Treat a configured GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT as sufficient credentials for
the vertex-ai auth type, in both the CLI pre-flight check and the core
model config validation, and leave the API key absent so the SDK
resolves ADC itself. The missing-credentials errors now mention the
keyless path instead of pointing only at envKey.

Fixes #9016

* fix(auth): select Vertex mode explicitly and keep de

    * fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials
    
    Vertex AI auth required an API key, so an ADC or service account setup
    could not start. Supplying a placeholder to satisfy the check made it
    worse: an explicitly passed key switches the Google SDK to Vertex
    Express mode, which clears the project and location and rejects the
    request with "API keys are not supported by this API".
    
    Treat a configured GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT as sufficient credentials for
    the vertex-ai auth type, in both the CLI pre-flight check and the core
    model config validation, and leave the API key absent so the SDK
    resolves ADC itself. The missing-credentials errors now mention the
    keyless path instead of pointing only at envKey.
    
    Fixes #9016
    
    * fix(auth): select Vertex mode explicitly and keep declared key vars authoritative
    
    Review follow-ups on the Vertex ADC change.
    
    Vertex mode no longer depends on the GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI side effect.
    Only the CLI pre-flight check writes that variable, and the startup call to it
    sits under the sandbox branch, so a plain interactive or ACP session built a
    client pointed at the Gemini API endpoint instead of Vertex. The flag is now
    derived from the auth type at construction, and left untouched for the other
    auth types so the SDK keeps its own environment fallback there.
    
    An entry that declares its own key variable no longer falls through to ADC when
    that variable is unset. It keeps failing on the declared variable, so a secret
    that failed to inject cannot silently authenticate as a different principal.
    The keyless hint is suppressed for those entries as well, since it would be
    advice that cannot work.
    
    The ACP pre-flight cell reports an indeterminate state for a keyless Vertex
    setup rather than a confirmed token: a configured project is routing
    configuration, not evidence that a credential resolves. All three gates now
    share one definition of a configured project, so whitespace is handled the same
    way everywhere, and the CLI missing-key message carries the same keyless hint as
    the core errors.
    
    Docs corrected on two counts: the environment-only row now says a keyless setup
    must select the auth type explicitly, since it is not inferred from the project
    alone, and the provider note names every key source the resolver folds in.
    
    ---------
    
    Co-authored-by: Shaojin Wen <shaojin.wensj@alibaba-inc.com>

evidence_units.claim: Commit fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430 identifies the prior failure: cloud authentication required an API key, while passing a placeholder key switched the SDK to an incompatible express mode; it states that project-only configuration should allow the SDK to resolve default credentials.

In the parent, CLI validation unconditionally called the API-key error resolver for the cloud auth type and rejected missing keys; the change first checks whether the selected model entry is eligible for default credentials and whether a nonblank project is configured.

The CLI eligibility check resolves the selected model-provider entry and excludes entries declaring envKey, preventing an unset declared secret from silently falling through to another principal. Project lookup considers process.env first and settings.env second.

Core introduces one project-configured predicate that trims the configured value, and its default-credential eligibility predicate requires the cloud auth type, no explicit apiKeyEnvKey, and a configured project.

Core model validation changes from rejecting every configuration without apiKey to accepting a missing key only when the default-credential eligibility predicate succeeds; explicit apiKeyEnvKey is forwarded to error construction.

SDK client construction maps the selected cloud auth type to vertexai=true when no explicit vertexai option overrides it and converts an empty API key to undefined, allowing SDK-side default credential resolution without relying on a prior environment side effect.

The CLI authentication entry point applies eligibility and project checks before session startup, while core validation independently applies the same keyless contract to resolved model configurations.

Missing-credential errors append the project/default-credential hint only for the cloud auth type when no explicit key variable was declared, avoiding unusable advice for other auth types and key-bound entries.

ACP preflight recognizes an eligible project-only configuration but reports status and hasToken as unknown because project routing configuration does not prove that a usable default credential resolves.

CLI tests specify acceptance for project-only environment and provider configurations, rejection when neither key nor project exists, preservation of an entry's declared envKey, and rejection of whitespace-only project values.

Core tests specify successful normal and strict validation for an eligible project-only configuration, rejection without a project, exclusion of other auth types, preservation of explicit key-variable requirements, and inclusion or suppression of the project hint according to eligibility.

title: Try credential sources in priority order until one authenticates
before: At parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, credential loading returned only the first parseable credential object. The default cached credential path preceded GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, so an expired or revoked default credential prevented the environment-provided credential from being considered. Encrypted-storage loading also returned directly, bypassing the environment-file fallback.
after: At f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297, credential discovery builds an ordered list from encrypted storage or the default cache followed by GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. Authentication evaluates candidates sequentially, uses a type-appropriate client, returns the first candidate that obtains a token, and logs and continues after loading or verification failures. The explicit cloud access-token override remains ahead of the candidate list, and later interactive or compute authentication remains available if no candidate succeeds.
diff: Replaced the single-result fetchCachedCredentials function with fetchCachedCredentialsList, which accumulates available credentials without stopping at the first parseable source and tolerates per-source failures. Added an ADC credential classifier, factored OAuth client construction and token-persistence callbacks into a helper, and changed initialization to verify each candidate sequentially with either GoogleAuth or OAuth2Client. Added a regression test proving that an expired default cached credential falls through to a valid GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS credential.

evidence_units.claim: Commit f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 is the implementation-bearing resolution for #28472, with parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7 and changes to oauth2.ts and oauth2.test.ts.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, changed_files_name_status, and git show --stat f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation returned immediately from encrypted storage or on the first parseable file in the ordered default-cache and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS paths, exposing only one credential to authentication.

The change replaces single-result credential loading with an ordered array: encrypted credentials are appended when enabled; otherwise the default cache is considered; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is then considered; malformed, unreadable, or unavailable sources are logged and skipped.
evidence_units.source: git diff c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7 f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 -- packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts, fetchCachedCredentialsList hunk

evidence_units.claim: Authentication now iterates the discovered credential list sequentially and returns only after a candidate obtains an access token; candidate verification exceptions are caught and the loop proceeds to the next candidate.

Typed non-authorized-user credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth.fromJSON, while ordinary cached OAuth credentials are applied to a fresh OAuth2Client and checked with getAccessToken followed by getTokenInfo.

OAuth client construction was centralized so every candidate OAuth client has the configured proxy and the token event handler that persists refreshed credentials and triggers post-authentication callbacks.
The exported getOauthClient entry point memoizes and invokes initOauthClient by authentication type, so the revised resolution loop governs callers using the public OAuth-client acquisition boundary.

The added regression test creates an expired default cached credential and a valid environment-file credential, makes access-token acquisition fail for the expired token, calls getOauthClient, and asserts that the environment credential is eventually applied.

semantic_action.intent: Make every configured fallback credential available to authentication while preserving source precedence.
semantic_action.pre_state: Credential sources have an established priority, but resolution returns a single credential and can therefore hide later fallbacks once an earlier source parses successfully.
semantic_action.post_state: Every successfully loaded credential is represented in priority order, and failure to load one source does not prevent later configured sources from being collected.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-credential-candidates-sequentially
candidate_atomics.title: Verify candidates sequentially and continue after rejection
candidate_atomics.description: Attempt each credential candidate with its appropriate authentication client, accepting the first verified candidate and treating an individual rejection as a recoverable fallback condition.

semantic_action.intent: Authenticate with the highest-priority usable credential instead of forcing reauthentication when a higher-priority cached credential is expired, revoked, or incompatible.
semantic_action.pre_state: An ordered set of credential candidates exists, but one candidate may fail token acquisition or server-side token validation.
semantic_action.post_state: The first candidate that successfully produces a usable token is returned; a failed candidate is logged and does not block verification of the next candidate.
semantic_action.validation: Make the first candidate fail token acquisition or token-info validation and make the next candidate succeed; assert that the succeeding credential is applied and returned through the public client-acquisition boundary.

candidate_workflows.name: restore-authentication-fallback-across-credential-sources
candidate_workflows.title: Restore authentication fallback across prioritized credential sources
candidate_workflows.description: Convert credential resolution from first-readable-source selection into ordered discovery followed by sequential, type-aware verification, without changing explicit overrides or downstream interactive authentication.

workflow_graph.goal: Return the highest-priority configured credential that can actually authenticate, while allowing a rejected cached credential to fall through to the next source.
when_to_use: Multiple credential sources have defined precedence and an earlier source can be present but expired, revoked, malformed, or otherwise unusable.
Authentication currently chooses the first readable credential rather than the first credential that passes its real verification oracle.

commit.subject: Optimize head‑truncation loop in `summarize_real`

limitations: No fabricated GitHub discussion metadata; implementation evidence must come from local git and checkout.

episode.title: Bound summarizer input in one forward pass and restore accurate tail-budget accounting
episode.before: At parent dc2d7b1dfe76b46a371e897aff76c3af76c73dd0, ChatSummary.summarize_real split oversized history into a head and preserved tail, then reversed both the head messages and their token-size pairs, accumulated messages from the end of the head up to the summarizer model's input limit, and reversed the retained messages again before summarizing. It also replaced the full sized-message list with the head-only slice and subsequently calculated tail_tokens from sized[split_index:], which was empty after that truncation; consequently the final fit decision did not account for the preserved tail's tokens.
episode.after: At 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa, summarize_real retains the full tokenized-message list, creates sized_head for the head, and selects a model-input-bounded prefix by accumulating (tokens, message) pairs directly in original order without list reversals. It computes tail_tokens from the untouched full sized list, returns summary plus tail only when their combined token count is below max_tokens, and otherwise recursively compacts the combined result with the existing depth guard.
episode.diff: The single-file implementation change in aider/history.py replaces head/sized reversal and index-based selection with a forward iteration over sized_head; preserves the original sized list; changes tail-token calculation to sum the original slice beginning at split_index; and keeps the existing 4096-token metadata fallback, 512-token safety reserve, direct-return threshold, and recursive compaction path. No tests were changed in the commit.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa has parent dc2d7b1dfe76b46a371e897aff76c3af76c73dd0, is titled "Optimize head‑truncation loop in `summarize_real`", and modifies only aider/history.py.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, changed_files_name_status

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation sliced sized down to the head, reversed head and sized, accumulated entries by index up to model_max_input_tokens, and reversed keep before calling summarize_all.

The changed implementation removes the list reversals and index loop, introduces sized_head = sized[:split_index], and accumulates tokens and messages directly with `for tokens, msg in sized_head` until the model input limit would be exceeded.

Because the parent reassigned sized to its head slice before evaluating `sized[split_index:]`, its tail-token sum was empty; the changed implementation leaves sized intact and calculates the preserved tail's tokens from the original `sized[split_index:]`.
evidence_units.source: git show 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa^:aider/history.py and git show 188e9e1114f0dfdeb95f9b1592bc81777a8226fa:aider/history.py, ChatSummary.summarize_real

evidence_units.claim: The implementation derives the summarizer input ceiling from the first model's max_input_tokens, falls back to 4096 when undefined, and reserves 512 tokens before selecting messages for summarize_all.

After summarizing the selected head, the implementation returns summary plus preserved tail only if their token total is below max_tokens; otherwise it recursively invokes summarize_real with depth incremented, while the existing depth greater than three guard eventually summarizes all remaining messages.

Application startup constructs ChatSummary with the weak and main models and with the configured or model-default maximum chat-history token budget, making summarize_real part of runtime chat-history compaction.

title: Make context-compaction and branch-summary requests resilient to transient stream failures
before: At parent 4b91ec66fd33026e6e44a0dca5a954a59abd3ee9, generated compaction summaries, split-turn prefix summaries, and branch summaries issued one model completion request. A transient retryable response such as stopReason="error" with errorMessage="terminated" immediately failed the structural session operation, even though agent-turn requests already had configurable retry settings. Retry backoff cancellation and summarization-specific retry lifecycle reporting were absent.
after: At 65dd2e0ed6c71bd61d698353c29f2de24968bf76, all generated compaction and branch-summary model calls can use the configured bounded retry policy. A shared helper retries only errors accepted by the existing transient-error classifier, applies exponential backoff, stops at maxRetries, fails fast for deterministic errors, and converts an abort during backoff into an aborted assistant response. Session and harness adapters pass retry policy and abort signals into summarization, emit retry lifecycle events, and allow the interactive UI and external consumers to observe retry scheduling, attempt restart, and completion.
diff: The merge adds reusable RetryPolicy, RetryCallbacks, abortable backoff, and retryAssistantCall in the AI utility layer; routes compaction history summaries, split-turn prefix summaries, and branch summaries through that retry boundary in both agent-harness and coding-agent implementations; supplies settings.retry from manual compaction, automatic compaction, and tree-navigation call sites; introduces typed retry lifecycle events and interactive status handling; and adds unit, harness, and issue-regression tests covering recovery, retry exhaustion, disabled policy, non-retryable errors, callback ordering, and abort during backoff.

commit.subject: Merge pull request #6901 from earendil-works/fix/issue-6647-retry-summary-requests-2
commit.body_excerpt: compaction & branch summarization follow retry policy

limitations: No fabricated GitHub discussion metadata; implementation evidence must come from local git and checkout.

episode.title: Make context-compaction and branch-summary requests resilient to transient stream failures
episode.before: At parent 4b91ec66fd33026e6e44a0dca5a954a59abd3ee9, generated compaction summaries, split-turn prefix summaries, and branch summaries issued one model completion request. A transient retryable response such as stopReason="error" with errorMessage="terminated" immediately failed the structural session operation, even though agent-turn requests already had configurable retry settings. Retry backoff cancellation and summarization-specific retry lifecycle reporting were absent.
episode.after: At 65dd2e0ed6c71bd61d698353c29f2de24968bf76, all generated compaction and branch-summary model calls can use the configured bounded retry policy. A shared helper retries only errors accepted by the existing transient-error classifier, applies exponential backoff, stops at maxRetries, fails fast for deterministic errors, and converts an abort during backoff into an aborted assistant response. Session and harness adapters pass retry policy and abort signals into summarization, emit retry lifecycle events, and allow the interactive UI and external consumers to observe retry scheduling, attempt restart, and completion.
episode.diff: The merge adds reusable RetryPolicy, RetryCallbacks, abortable backoff, and retryAssistantCall in the AI utility layer; routes compaction history summaries, split-turn prefix summaries, and branch summaries through that retry boundary in both agent-harness and coding-agent implementations; supplies settings.retry from manual compaction, automatic compaction, and tree-navigation call sites; introduces typed retry lifecycle events and interactive status handling; and adds unit, harness, and issue-regression tests covering recovery, retry exhaustion, disabled policy, non-retryable errors, callback ordering, and abort during backoff.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned merge commit 65dd2e0ed6c71bd61d698353c29f2de24968bf76 has first parent 4b91ec66fd33026e6e44a0dca5a954a59abd3ee9 and states that compaction and branch summarization follow retry policy.

The AI utility layer defines a retry policy and callbacks, then implements a bounded loop that classifies retryable assistant errors, computes exponential delays, supports abortable backoff, and reports success, exhaustion, or abort.
Before the change, agent-harness compaction history summaries, split-turn prefix summaries, and branch summaries called Models.completeSimple directly without a retry policy.

Agent-harness adds completeSimpleWithRetries and routes ordinary compaction summaries, split-turn prefix summaries, and branch summaries through it while propagating retry policy, callbacks, and the operation abort signal.

Coding-agent exports completeSummarization as the common completion boundary and wraps either the configured stream function or the simple completion function with retryAssistantCall; all compaction summary variants pass retry policy and callbacks through this boundary.

Manual compaction and automatic threshold/overflow compaction obtain the configured retry settings and pass operation-specific callbacks and the existing compaction abort signal into summary generation.

Default branch summarization during tree navigation receives the configured retry settings, branch-summary retry callbacks, and the existing branch-summary abort signal; extension-provided summaries bypass model generation.

Coding-agent maps retry callbacks to typed summarization_retry_scheduled, summarization_retry_attempt_start, and summarization_retry_finished events, preserving compaction reason or branch-summary source for consumers.
Agent-harness accepts an optional retry policy, emits operation-tagged retry lifecycle events, and supplies those callbacks to generated compaction and branch-summary operations.

Retry utility tests specify immediate success, no retry for abort or quota errors, disabled-policy behavior, bounded exhaustion, recovery before exhaustion, callback ordering, and aborting a pending backoff.

Harness tests specify successful recovery of compaction and branch-summary operations, no retry for non-retryable errors, exhaustion at the configured budget, and operation-tagged retry event sequences.

The issue regression test reproduces transient mid-stream "terminated" failures and specifies that compaction succeeds after retries, fails fast for quota or disabled retry, stops after maxRetries, and can abort a long backoff.
Interactive mode displays the transient error and retry countdown, restores the branch-summary or compaction status when a retry attempt starts, and clears retry status when the loop finishes.

The committed regression oracle expects three model calls for two transient failures followed by success, one call for non-retryable or disabled cases, three calls for maxRetries=2 exhaustion, and an aborted compaction when cancellation interrupts backoff.

The implementation change is behavior-bearing rather than documentation-only: the first-parent diff changes retry utilities, both summarization implementations, session/harness call sites, event contracts, UI handling, and tests.

when_to_use: A context compaction, truncation, checkpoint, or branch-preservation operation depends on a model-generated summary.
A transient stream or transport failure currently aborts the entire structural context operation on its first failed request.
The runtime already has, or can accept, a bounded retry policy and an operation cancellation signal.
anti_goals: Do not retry context-overflow, quota, billing, authentication, or other errors rejected by the transient-error classifier.
Do not create an unbounded retry loop or silently ignore the configured retry budget.
Do not retry summaries supplied by hooks, extensions, caches, or callers when no model request is made.
Do not change summary selection, token budgeting, retained-tail boundaries, prompts, or persistence semantics merely to add request resilience.
not_applicable_when: The failure is caused by deterministic summary preparation, invalid session structure, or an unusable context boundary rather than a transient assistant request error.
The operation has no model-generated summary request.
The system cannot classify failed assistant responses or cannot cancel a pending retry delay safely.
inputs: Retry policy with enabled, maxRetries, and baseDelayMs
Cancellation signal scoped to the structural operation
Scripted completion responses for success, transient failure, terminal failure, and abort
workflow_graph.entry_state: Context-summary preparation succeeds, but at least one generated summary path performs a single request whose transient failure terminates compaction or branch preservation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All generated summary paths use the same bounded retry invariant, retain existing operation cancellation and supplied-summary behavior, expose retry lifecycle state, and satisfy recovery and terminal-case regression oracles.

steps.condition: A failed assistant response can be classified as transient or terminal and the caller can provide a retry policy.
steps.validation: Utility-level scripted responses prove bounded attempts, exponential-delay callbacks, fail-fast exclusions, successful recovery, and abortable backoff.

steps.condition: Execute only for model-generated summaries; bypass when a hook or extension already supplied the summary.
steps.validation: Entry-point tests prove compaction and branch-summary recovery after transient failures and unchanged failure behavior when retry is disabled, exhausted, aborted, or terminal.

steps.condition: The host exposes operation events or interactive status and retry delays are externally observable.
steps.validation: Subscriber tests verify operation-tagged scheduled/start/finished order; UI handlers restore the underlying compaction or branch-summary status and clear retry state on completion.

title: Cap shell-output truncation by the remaining model context budget
before: At parent commit 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returned only the configured threshold. The shell-tool scheduler already used that getter when deciding how many output characters to retain, so the effective threshold did not shrink when the preceding prompt had consumed most of the model's context window.
after: At commit b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returns the smaller of the configured threshold and four times the model token limit minus the latest prompt token count. Thus, when shell-output truncation is enabled, the existing scheduler receives a context-aware character threshold while retaining a lower default or custom configured cap.
diff: The change imports the model token-limit lookup and UI telemetry service into the configuration module, replaces the fixed threshold getter with Math.min(4 * (tokenLimit(model) - lastPromptTokenCount), configuredThreshold), and adds focused tests for a remaining-context cap below the default, preservation of the default when it is lower, and both branches with a custom configured threshold. The scheduler call site and truncation mechanism are unchanged.

episode.title: Cap shell-output truncation by the remaining model context budget
episode.before: At parent commit 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returned only the configured threshold. The shell-tool scheduler already used that getter when deciding how many output characters to retain, so the effective threshold did not shrink when the preceding prompt had consumed most of the model's context window.
episode.after: At commit b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returns the smaller of the configured threshold and four times the model token limit minus the latest prompt token count. Thus, when shell-output truncation is enabled, the existing scheduler receives a context-aware character threshold while retaining a lower default or custom configured cap.
episode.diff: The change imports the model token-limit lookup and UI telemetry service into the configuration module, replaces the fixed threshold getter with Math.min(4 * (tokenLimit(model) - lastPromptTokenCount), configuredThreshold), and adds focused tests for a remaining-context cap below the default, preservation of the default when it is lower, and both branches with a custom configured threshold. The scheduler call site and truncation mechanism are unchanged.

evidence_units.claim: Commit b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 8379, has parent 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88, and changes only config.ts and config.test.ts.
In the parent state, getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returned this.truncateToolOutputThreshold without consulting model capacity or prompt usage.

The resolved state computes the returned threshold as Math.min(4 * (tokenLimit(this.model) - uiTelemetryService.getLastPromptTokenCount()), this.truncateToolOutputThreshold), with the comment that one token is estimated as four characters.

The configured truncation threshold remains the caller-provided value when present, otherwise DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_TOOL_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD; the change modifies the getter rather than this initialization contract.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/config/config.ts, constructor initialization of truncateToolOutputThreshold

evidence_units.claim: The token-limit helper maps a model identifier to its context-token capacity and falls back to DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT for unlisted models.
The telemetry service exposes getLastPromptTokenCount(), returning its stored latest-prompt token count, which starts at zero and can be reset to zero.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/telemetry/uiTelemetry.ts, UiTelemetryService state and accessors

evidence_units.claim: For successful string output from the shell tool, the scheduler checks that truncation is enabled and that threshold and line limits are positive, then passes getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() to truncateAndSaveToFile; this call site is unchanged from the parent.

title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs without exposing partial state
before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, fork creation wrote the destination header directly to its final JSONL path and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, name, and labels one mutation at a time. Torn-tail recovery similarly overwrote the original session file directly with its valid prefix, so an interrupted repair could damage the only persisted copy.
after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem contract provides atomic rename-with-replacement. Fork semantics are first converted into a complete ordered mutation plan, and both fork creation and torn-tail repair build a sibling temporary file before atomically renaming it into place. Population or rename failures remove the temporary file and leave the destination absent or unchanged.
diff: The change adds an atomic rename capability to the filesystem abstraction and Node implementation; introduces a shared stage-then-rename publication helper with best-effort temporary cleanup; moves fork mutation derivation into session state for reuse by memory and JSONL backends; delegates JSONL fork publication to storage so the entire header and mutation sequence is staged before visibility; and changes torn-tail truncation to publish a staged valid prefix. Failure-injection tests cover staging failure, rename failure, preservation of the original during failed repair, temporary-file cleanup, and successful reopening with fork state intact.

episode.title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs without exposing partial state
episode.before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, fork creation wrote the destination header directly to its final JSONL path and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, name, and labels one mutation at a time. A failure during that sequence could leave a discoverable partial fork. Torn-tail recovery similarly overwrote the original session file directly with its valid prefix, so an interrupted repair could damage the only persisted copy.
episode.after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem contract provides atomic rename-with-replacement. Fork semantics are first converted into a complete ordered mutation plan, and both fork creation and torn-tail repair build a sibling temporary file before atomically renaming it into place. Population or rename failures remove the temporary file and leave the destination absent or unchanged.
episode.diff: The change adds an atomic rename capability to the filesystem abstraction and Node implementation; introduces a shared stage-then-rename publication helper with best-effort temporary cleanup; moves fork mutation derivation into session state for reuse by memory and JSONL backends; delegates JSONL fork publication to storage so the entire header and mutation sequence is staged before visibility; and changes torn-tail truncation to publish a staged valid prefix. evidence_units.claim: Commit a838c069 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 7707 and changes ten agent implementation and test files.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0] and commit_show_stat; git show --stat a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, the repository created the final fork file immediately, then copied entries, lanes, name, and labels through separate awaited appends, allowing a failed sequence to leave a partial destination.
Before the change, detection of a malformed final JSONL line repaired the file by writing the valid prefix directly over the original path.
The filesystem contract now exposes atomic rename with destination replacement, and the Node implementation resolves both paths, invokes rename, and reports source-path failures.
Tests verify that rename removes the source, replaces existing destination content, reports a missing source path, and leaves the destination unchanged on failure.

The publication helper populates a deterministic sibling .tmp file, renames it over the destination only after population completes, and removes the temporary file on population or rename failure while preserving the original error.

Session state derives a complete, consecutively sequenced fork mutation list containing the selected entries, lane pointers, optional name, and labels; invalid branch targets are rejected before publication.

The repository prepares only the destination header and path, then delegates the fork to source storage; JSONL storage stages the header and every derived mutation before atomic publication and reloads the published file.
The in-memory backend consumes the same fork mutation derivation as the JSONL backend, keeping fork selection and metadata-copy semantics aligned across storage implementations.
Successful fork tests verify persisted message counts and verify that a reopened tree fork retains entries, lanes, name, labels, and excludes records.
Failure-injection tests verify that append failure during staging and atomic rename failure publish no fork, keep only the source session listed, and leave no .tmp file.
When replay detects a parse failure confined to the physical final line, storage stages the valid prefix through the atomic publication helper rather than overwriting the session directly.
A repair failure injected after truncating the staged file causes open to fail while the original torn session remains byte-for-byte unchanged and the temporary file is removed.

title: Preserve paired tool-call identifiers for protocol versions that require them
before: At parent 786c76cb76bea452fa7287cc1014c4a3d3cad2b1, the shared Google message converter treated only model IDs beginning with `claude-` or `gpt-oss-` as requiring explicit tool-call IDs. after: At cbaca60389f5d7097a43c95f56a19d344ecf2195, the requirement predicate also recognizes parsed Gemini major versions greater than or equal to 3. Existing converter branches governed by that predicate therefore emit the same normalized identifiers on function-call and function-response parts for Gemini 3 across the Google Generative AI and Vertex adapters, while Gemini 2.5 continues omitting them.
diff: The implementation adds the existing Gemini major-version parser to `requiresToolCallId`, extending the predicate by one condition without changing the serialization branches. Tests add paired tool results, verify IDs on both sides of two tool interactions for multiple Gemini 3 model IDs and both adapter APIs, verify omission for Gemini 2.5, and directly test the expanded predicate while retaining prior Claude and GPT-OSS behavior.

commit.subject: Harden Code Mode tool-call completeness tracking (#44472)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Reused call IDs, ambiguous exec/wait associations, and missing history can make tool-call completeness claims unreliable. Truncating one cell's recorded calls should also preserve completeness for unrelated cells.

## What changed

- Track observed call and runtime cell IDs with bounded memory, including call IDs from initial history, and withhold completeness when evidence is missing or ambiguous.
- Validate exec/wait input-output associations and keep invalidated completeness from returning on retries. Withhold wait completeness after resume or fork, where runtime cell IDs can be reused.
- Keep truncation markers and omission counts local to each output, clearing completeness across the affected cell while preserving unrelated cells within the metadata budget.
- Refresh recording

Recording enablement can be refreshed independently from execution features while legacy reloads preserve the live recorder.
episode.diff: The change modifies 12 files with 1,772 insertions and 638 deletions. It adds a bounded monotonic SeenIds filter; passes InitialHistory into recorder construction; adds origin, runtime-cell, duplicate-call, and exec/wait association checks; makes retained completeness fail closed across retries and compaction; rewrites request-budget handling around per-output omission markers and cell-scoped completion invalidation; adds runtime recorder refresh handling; and adds unit and integration regressions for reused IDs, missing or paginated history, mismatched wrappers, resumed waits, compaction, unrelated truncation, and runtime enablement.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit identifies reused call IDs, ambiguous exec/wait associations, missing history, and cross-cell truncation effects as causes of unreliable completeness claims, and states that the resolution tracks IDs, validates associations, localizes truncation, and refreshes recording enablement.
The parent recorder constructor accepted only feature state, allocated optional immutable recorder storage, did not index history, and unconditionally changed a registered cell to Started.

SeenIds uses a bounded monotonic bitmap with separate call-ID and runtime-cell namespaces, indexes identifiers from normal and compacted initial history subject to entry and byte limits, and reports history_ids_indexed=false when complete indexing cannot be established.

Recorder initialization now consumes InitialHistory, permits wait-completion proof only for new or cleared history, and starts a cell only when its runtime ID and origin are fresh and history identifiers were successfully indexed; otherwise it makes the cell incomplete.

Repeated wrapper origins, direct call IDs, runtime-cell IDs, and nested call IDs invalidate completion; invalidation is propagated to retained records associated with the affected origin or runtime cell.

Prompt attachment counts outputs, records only unique input positions, validates that each exec or wait input precedes and semantically matches its output, rejects direct-call collisions, and prevents a retained incomplete record from becoming complete again after inventory or association evidence is lost.

Prompt attachment withholds completion for ordinary wait outputs when the session came from resumed or forked history because runtime cell handles may be reused, while direct exec output can still be certified from locally observed evidence.

Protocol budgeting now tracks damaged cell identifiers, clears completeness across only those cells, sheds optional result metadata and sources before call evidence, and replaces an over-budget output's own calls with a local omission marker rather than using a global omission fallback.
Session construction passes initial history to the recorder, making historical call identifiers part of the completion-proof boundary.

Normal runtime configuration refresh updates recorder enablement independently of execution features, while legacy configuration reload explicitly skips recorder refresh to preserve the current live recorder.

Recorder-level regressions cover lossless completion, paginated history, forked waits, wrapper mismatch, reused origins, direct-ID collision, truncation after compaction, missing historical evidence, and preservation of unrelated complete outputs under overflow.

End-to-end Code Mode regressions exercise ID knowledge after compaction, runtime recording enablement, recorder preservation across refresh, resumed wait cell reuse, and survival of an unrelated complete call during truncation.

Protocol tests assert that completeness is host-only and fail-closed, raw result metadata is shed before stronger evidence, and metadata budgeting retains evidence without allowing one damaged cell to certify another output.

The implementation supplies layered regression oracles at bounded-ID unit, recorder/request-metadata, protocol-budgeting, and end-to-end Code Mode levels; the evidence bundle does not report an executed test command or status-check result.

candidate_workflows.title: Harden structured tool-call completion proofs
candidate_workflows.description: A fail-closed resolution chain for completion metadata that crosses session history, asynchronous exec/wait wrappers, retries, compaction, and bounded prompt serialization.

workflow_graph.goal: Emit a positive structured completion claim only when the host retains an unambiguous, lossless chain from a fresh invocation through its nested calls and matching output, while preserving valid claims for unrelated cells.
when_to_use: A host records nested tool activity and exposes a structured completeness marker to a later model request or downstream consumer.
Invocation or runtime identifiers can be reused across retries, compaction, resume, fork, or asynchronous wait operations.
Recorded evidence is subject to per-call or aggregate serialization budgets.
Recording policy can change during a long-lived session.
anti_goals: Do not change tool execution availability, dispatch gates, or nested-tool behavior merely to change recording policy.
Do not infer completeness from a successful wrapper callback, terminal wait, or retained marker when association or inventory evidence is missing.
Do not discard trustworthy metadata for unrelated cells solely because one cell exceeded a budget.
Do not use unbounded sets or unbounded hashing to prove identifier freshness.
not_applicable_when: The metadata is informational only and no consumer interprets it as a complete inventory or proof.
Invocation identifiers and output associations are guaranteed unique and immutable by a stronger external protocol, with no retries, resume, fork, compaction, or truncation boundary.
No host-side execution evidence can be inspected; in that case a positive completion contract cannot be established.
inputs: Initial session history, including compacted replacement history when available

title: Halt repeated variants of read-only repository inspection commands
before: At parent commit 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620, the always-on loop detector recognized consecutive calls only when the tool name and complete arguments were identical, plus a per-turn tool-call cap. Variants such as repository status, summary diff, revision-only diff, and tracked-file listing produced different argument hashes, so a consecutive sequence of semantically equivalent read-only inspections could continue without the always-on detector identifying stagnation.
after: At commit 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da, shell tool requests are classified into a common repository-overview-inspection bucket only when every shell-chain segment is a read-only status, diff, or tracked-file listing and any diff is revision/option based rather than path-specific. Eight consecutive bucketed requests halt the run through the always-on safety tier, record and emit a dedicated loop type, clear pending calls, and expose a human-readable CLI reason. Nonmatching calls and retries reset the streak; session disable is honored; write-bearing, mixed-purpose, non-repository, and file-specific review commands fail open.
diff: The change adds a semantic classifier and consecutive-streak state to the loop-detection service, invokes the new check between the identical-call guard and hard per-turn cap, resets its state at progress/retry/prompt boundaries, introduces a dedicated telemetry enum value, and propagates that reason through the existing client halt path and non-interactive message formatter. It adds regression coverage for variant and newline-separated inspection loops, threshold behavior, reset behavior, session disable, and false-positive exclusions. Five files changed with 461 insertions and 16 deletions.

title: Strip truncated tool-argument fragments prefixed by a bare tool name
before: At parent commit 41c17d9b5e1299b404700f86d6abad5cd406f3b6, the unterminated-tool-call sanitizer recognized argument-tag fragments only when an <arg_key> or <arg_value> tag itself began the line (apart from whitespace), or when an argument closer ended the line. A truncated serialization such as "process_manage<arg_key>action</arg_key>..." therefore escaped sanitization because the bare tool name preceded the first tag.
after: At cf8b08edac3a78feb4b9db0c20a62934c3a6c49d, the line-boundary alternative accepts an optional prefix composed only of identifier-like characters [\w.:-] before an argument tag. Both display and storage sanitizers consequently remove bare-name-prefixed truncated tool-call fragments while retaining preceding visible text; existing tests continue to require that prose containing spaced inline argument-tag examples and subsequent prose remain intact.
diff: The implementation changed one regular-expression alternative from matching optional whitespace immediately followed by an argument tag to matching optional whitespace, then zero or more identifier-like characters, then the tag. Comments document the bounded prefix and prose-preservation intent. Two parameterized regression cases were added: one complete name-prefixed argument fragment and one fragment cut inside its argument value. The cases run against both the final-display sanitizer and the stored-content sanitizer.

title: Centralize hierarchical project trust before loading effect-bearing resources
before: At parent 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84, trust decisions were exact-directory lookups. The main runtime had its own trust resolver, while package commands used a separate simpler resolver that honored only an explicit override, absence of trust inputs, or an exact saved true decision; the config command defaulted to trusted. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md counted as trust-triggering inputs and were omitted when a project was untrusted. There was no global defaultProjectTrust policy, no parent-directory inheritance, and package/config commands did not run project_trust extension hooks.
after: At d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd, one resolver applies ordered trust sources across runtime, package, and config paths: explicit command override; automatic trust when no effect-bearing project inputs exist; a project_trust extension result loaded during an untrusted bootstrap pass; the nearest persisted directory decision; the global-only defaultProjectTrust policy; then an interactive prompt or fail-closed denial without UI. Persisted decisions can apply to a parent directory and be inherited by descendants, with child overrides removable. The resolved decision is installed into SettingsManager before project packages, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, system prompts, or local package-setting writes are processed. Passive AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md context remains readable regardless of trust and no longer triggers a trust prompt.
diff: The merge adds core/project-trust.ts and reusable CLI trust/startup UI modules; extends the trust store with nearest-ancestor lookup, multi-path updates, parent-scope options, and inherited-decision metadata; adds a global-only defaultProjectTrust setting; extracts an untrusted extension bootstrap operation from ResourceLoader; routes normal runtime, package commands, and config commands through the same asynchronous trust resolver; preserves denial of trust-gated resources and local writes while removing context files from that gated set; and adds tests for precedence, extension hooks, inherited scopes, boundary classification, and non-interactive isolation.

episode.title: Centralize hierarchical project trust before loading effect-bearing resources
episode.before: At parent 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84, trust decisions were exact-directory lookups. The main runtime had its own trust resolver, while package commands used a separate simpler resolver that honored only an explicit override, absence of trust inputs, or an exact saved true decision; the config command defaulted to trusted. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md counted as trust-triggering inputs and were omitted when a project was untrusted. There was no global defaultProjectTrust policy, no parent-directory inheritance, and package/config commands did not run project_trust extension hooks.
episode.after: At d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd, one resolver applies ordered trust sources across runtime, package, and config paths: explicit command override; automatic trust when no effect-bearing project inputs exist; a project_trust extension result loaded during an untrusted bootstrap pass; the nearest persisted directory decision; the global-only defaultProjectTrust policy; then an interactive prompt or fail-closed denial without UI. Persisted decisions can apply to a parent directory and be inherited by descendants, with child overrides removable. The resolved decision is installed into SettingsManager before project packages, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, system prompts, or local package-setting writes are processed. Passive AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md context remains readable regardless of trust and no longer triggers a trust prompt.
episode.diff: The merge adds core/project-trust.ts and reusable CLI trust/startup UI modules; extends the trust store with nearest-ancestor lookup, multi-path updates, parent-scope options, and inherited-decision metadata; adds a global-only defaultProjectTrust setting; extracts an untrusted extension bootstrap operation from ResourceLoader; routes normal runtime, package commands, and config commands through the same asynchronous trust resolver; preserves denial of trust-gated resources and local writes while removing context files from that gated set; and adds tests for precedence, extension hooks, inherited scopes, boundary classification, and non-interactive isolation.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned merge commit d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd merged PR #5549 with subject 'feat(ui): Improved project approval settings' and first parent 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The first-parent change adds project-trust policy and startup UI modules and modifies trust storage, resource loading, settings, package/config commands, interactive trust selection, and focused tests.

Before the change, ProjectTrustStore.get read only the normalized current-directory key, trust inputs included AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, package commands used an independent synchronous resolver, and config commands defaulted projectTrusted to true.

The centralized resolver evaluates explicit override first, returns trusted when no trust inputs exist, then consults project_trust extensions, persisted trust, global defaultProjectTrust, and finally UI; absence or cancellation of UI resolves to false.
Trust lookup walks from the normalized working directory toward the filesystem root and returns the nearest boolean decision; batched updates can set parent decisions and delete child overrides.
Trust-triggering inputs are limited to a local .pi directory or an ancestor .agents/skills directory; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are not classified as trust inputs.

ResourceLoader performs a bootstrap pass with project trust forced false, reloads settings, and loads only the current non-project extension set before resolving trust; it then installs the decision, reloads settings, and resolves normal resources.

Package and config commands create SettingsManager as untrusted, optionally bootstrap project_trust extensions, call the centralized resolver with the global default, install the result, and reject local package-setting writes when untrusted.

The main runtime calls the centralized resolver from ResourceLoader.reload and supplies the command override, global default policy, bootstrap extension result, and a UI context whose availability depends on the active mode.

Trust-store tests prove nearest-parent inheritance, closest-child override precedence, removal of a child override to restore parent inheritance, and rejection of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md as trust-triggering inputs.

Package-command tests prove that the global default can trust project packages, project_trust extensions can authorize package commands, and an explicit persisted false decision overrides a global always default.
Settings tests prove defaultProjectTrust is read only from global settings and invalid values fail safely to ask.
Resource-loader tests prove that an untrusted project still contributes AGENTS.md context while project system prompts, extensions, skills, prompts, and themes remain excluded.
A spawned-CLI test proves an untrusted non-interactive help invocation does not install project packages or emit their installation output.
Trust-selector tests prove inherited decisions are labeled with their source path and selecting parent trust produces a parent true update plus deletion of the current-directory override.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure project-local effects execute or mutate state only after one consistently resolved authorization decision, while passive context remains available and headless ambiguity fails closed.
when_to_use: A tool discovers project-local configuration, packages, plugins, scripts, skills, prompts, themes, or similar resources that can execute code or change runtime behavior.
Multiple entry points such as the main runtime, package commands, and configuration commands must share the same project authorization semantics.
Authorization may be supplied by explicit overrides, extension hooks, persisted directory policy, global defaults, or an interactive user decision.
anti_goals: Do not execute project-local hooks or install project packages to determine whether that same project is trusted.

not_applicable_when: The project exposes no local input capable of executing code, installing dependencies, mutating configuration, or injecting runtime resources.

inputs: Canonical working directory and its ancestor chain
